pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which word needs a capital letter? (1 mark)
   A. road
   B. market
   C. river
   D. Nairobi

2. Which sentence should be read with a rising voice in English? (1 mark)
   A. Are you coming to school?
   B. We go to school.
   C. You are coming to school.
   D. Come to school.

3. What is a product? (1 mark)
   A. A time
   B. A poem
   C. A thing made or grown for sale
   D. A place

4. What is a cue in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. A drawing
   B. A full stop
   C. The last words of the person before you
   D. A title

5. Which of these is an adjective in Fresh sweet oranges? (1 mark)
   A. sale
   B. oranges
   C. for
   D. sweet

6. What should a real-life experience description include? (1 mark)
   A. Who, what, when, where and how you felt
   B. Only a title
   C. Nothing
   D. Only a number

7. What does inferring meaning mean? (1 mark)
   A. Copying words
   B. Spelling backwards
   C. Ignoring the word
   D. Working out meaning from clues

8. What should you use to fill a form unless told otherwise? (1 mark)
   A. A pen
   B. A crayon
   C. A chalk
   D. A finger

9. What is a poem's title? (1 mark)
   A. Its page
   B. Its rhyme
   C. Its name
   D. Its last line

10. What should you do first when a call is answered? (1 mark)
   A. Hang up
   B. Greet politely
   C. Shout
   D. Ask for money

11. Why should you ask an adult before giving your address on an online form? (1 mark)
   A. To waste time
   B. No reason
   C. To make it longer
   D. To stay safe

12. Why do we use punctuation marks? (1 mark)
   A. To make pages heavy
   B. To make writing clear
   C. To hide meaning
   D. To use up ink

13. A word bank is (1 mark)
   A. a type of song
   B. a place for money
   C. a kind of poem
   D. a class list of useful words on one theme

14. How should a proverb be used in a composition? (1 mark)
   A. Anywhere at all
   B. In a way that fits the story
   C. With no meaning
   D. Only at the start

15. Which is a poem's mood if it is joyful? (1 mark)
   A. Sleepy
   B. Sad
   C. Happy
   D. Angry

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Read: The nurse bandaged the wound gently and the blood stopped. What does wound mean? Give two clues. (3 marks)

17. Name two digital devices and give a use of each. (2 marks)

18. Give three parts of a news item. (3 marks)

19. Describe how a panel discussion is organised. (4 marks)

20. Give three steps for telling a story fluently. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Nairobi
   Names of towns begin with capital letters.

2. A — Are you coming to school?
   It is a question.

3. C — A thing made or grown for sale
   A product is a thing for sale.

4. C — The last words of the person before you
   You come in when you hear your cue.

5. D — sweet
   Sweet describes the oranges.

6. A — Who, what, when, where and how you felt
   These details make it clear.

7. D — Working out meaning from clues
   Inferring uses clues in the context.

8. A — A pen
   A pen gives clear permanent writing.

9. C — Its name
   The title names the poem.

10. B — Greet politely
   A greeting begins the call.

11. D — To stay safe
   Personal details should be protected.

12. B — To make writing clear
   Punctuation helps readers understand.

13. D — a class list of useful words on one theme
   A vocabulary bank collects words by topic.

14. B — In a way that fits the story
   A proverb should match the lesson of the story.

15. C — Happy
   A joyful poem has a happy mood.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: A wound is an injury. Clues are the nurse, bandaged and blood.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and two marks for clues, awarding one for each up to two.

17. (2 marks)
   Answer: Phone for calling, radio for hearing news, camera for taking photos (any two with uses).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each device with its use.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: Headline, lead, details, quote (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

19. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a topic, a moderator and panel members, panel members give opinions in turn, the audience asks questions, the moderator summarises.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

20. (3 marks)
   Answer: Know the story well, speak clearly, keep a steady pace, change your voice for characters, look at the audience, end with the lesson.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.
